subject: Recap & next steps: Avatech deployment constraints and isolation preferences
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Holt <erin@avatech.com>
Cc: Dana Collins <dana.collins@avatech.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: Avatech deployment constraints and isolation preferences

Thanks again for the time today, Erin — great conversation. Quick recap of what I heard and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

1) Goals and constraints
- Primary requirement: strict separation of customer data from any multi-tenant caches and no persistent model artifacts stored on shared infrastructure.
- Must support BYOK (customer-managed keys) and audit-grade access logs for all inference requests.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~250 concurrent sessions, average 800 tokens/session; peak bursts up to 1.2k concurrent sessions.

2) Current leaning
- You and Dana indicated a strong preference toward a private network boundary (VPC) because of regulatory comfort and control over key management.

3) Clarifying questions (can you confirm?):
- When you say "no persistent model artifacts," do you mean no writes of KV/cache to shared disks and records of raw prompt text in long-term storage?
- Are you expecting us to operate in your VPC (Redwood Private control plane + customer VPC), or are you considering an on-prem appliance for air-gapped requirements?
- For BYOK: do you need HSM-backed keys or KMS integration is sufficient?

4) Proposed immediate next steps
- If you confirm the storage/keys expectations, we can put together two concrete proposals: (A) Private VPC deployment with BYOK + audit logging + optional dedicated GPU pool behind the VPC, (B) Dedicated-hosted offering with strict cache isolation and per-customer encrypted volumes. I will include rough cost/latency tradeoffs and a proposed PoC plan.

Attachments: Avatech data flow diagram (you shared) and the security questionnaire draft you asked for — I'll send an editable copy if you'd like.

Can you loop in procurement (if procurement will own the contract) and confirm the BYOK/HSM preference? Happy to set a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the two proposal options.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0138

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Avatech deployment constraints and isolation preferences

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the succinct summary. A few clarifications from our side (Dana added comments inline):

- "No persistent model artifacts": correct. We cannot have raw prompts or customer PII landing in any multi-tenant long-term storage. Short-lived memory (in-RAM / ephemeral KV) is acceptable if it never persists to shared disk and is cleared per-session.
- Deployment preference: our default preference is Private VPC (control plane outside, compute in our VPC). If a fully air-gapped on-prem appliance is required, that would be handled as a separate procurement track — likely a longer timeline.
- BYOK: our security team prefers HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3) for key material; KMS is acceptable if it is backed by customer HSM and we have clear rotation/audit policies.
- Audit/logging: must capture request metadata, timestamp, model version, and a non-reversible request hash. Raw prompts should not persist beyond the ephemeral processing window unless redaction/tokenization is performed first.

Dana also writes: "We will need evidence of per-request logging, key usage logs, and a description of how you guarantee cache eviction. If Redwood can provide a short technical note on cache behavior (ephemeral vs persisted) that would speed legal/security review."

Procurement is cc'd — they will advise on commercial/compliance milestones once we see the two option proposals.

Happy to do a quick follow-up Tues/Wed next week; procurement will confirm availability.

—Erin
Erin Holt
Head of Product, Avatech
erin@avatech.com

Subject: Fwd: Avatech constraints — need dedicated vs private recommendation

Forwarding the thread from Avatech — they explicitly want: Private VPC compute, HSM-backed BYOK, and no persistent raw prompts on shared storage. Dana asked for a short technical note on cache behavior and eviction guarantees. Attached their data flow diagram and the security questionnaire we started.

High-level asks for the team:
- Monica: can you draft a 1-page technical note describing how our runtime handles KV/prefix caching, where data lives at each stage (RAM vs disk), and the eviction lifecycle? Include how we would configure the runtime in a Private VPC deployment to ensure no shared disk persistence.
- Rishi: estimate performance delta (p90 latency and token throughput) for Private VPC with a dedicated GPU pool vs Dedicated-hosted option (isolation at infra level but managed by Redwood). Include any limits we should flag for their concurrency profile.
- Markus: I think this will be an Enterprise track — want your guidance on pricing guardrails and a PoC cadence (2-week PoC with gating criteria?).

Timeline: Avatech hopes to see our two proposals early next week. Can each of you reply with your pieces by Monday EOD so I can assemble and send Tues morning PST.

Thanks —
Vanessa

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Avatech constraints — need dedicated vs private recommendation

Thanks Vanessa — below are the concise items we can include in the Avatech tech note and the quick recommendation. I kept it high-level but concrete so it can be handed to Dana/security: 

1) Cache & KV behavior (short summary for security team)\- Runtime defaults: KV/prefix cache is in-memory and per-session; by default we do not write KV caches to disk.
- Ephemeral mode (recommended for Avatech Private VPC): configure runtime with "ephemeral-kv=true" and "persist-to-disk=false". This guarantees caches never land on mounted volumes.
- Eviction and lifecycle: per-session TTL + explicit eviction on session close. We maintain no long-term prompt logs in the runtime; only non-reversible hashes recorded in the audit stream (configurable).

2) BYOK and key handling\- We support KMS-based integrations and can be configured to use customer-managed keys backed by HSM (Bring-Your-Own-Key). For Private VPC, key operations are proxied through their KMS endpoint; Redwood does not retain raw key material.
- Logging: we can emit key usage events to a customer-owned logging sink (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk) and include KMS request IDs in audit logs.

3) Private VPC vs Dedicated (tradeoffs)\- Private VPC (recommended): Compute runs in customer VPC/subnets under network controls; best for strict compliance because it limits network exposure and allows customer-side KMS/HSM integration. Slightly higher setup time and network egress considerations; we estimate +5—10% p95 latency vs hosted.
- Dedicated-hosted: Managed by Redwood on isolated GPU pools; offers faster setup and simpler upgrades but relies on our infrastructure for key-proxying and requires stronger contractual commitments around cache non-persistence. Lower latency by ~5% on average vs Private VPC, but potentially less comfortable for audit teams.

4) PoC recommendation and gating\- Recommended PoC: 2 weeks in Private VPC with a small dedicated GPU pool (2 GPUs) and the following gates: HSM integration test, audit log delivery to customer sink, and stress test to validate p95 latency at 1.2k concurrent sessions.
- Deliverables: 1-page tech note (see above), a cost-latency comparison table, and a PoC runbook + success criteria.

I can draft the 1-page tech note and the PoC runbook today — will send as a PDF and a copy-paste-able doc for procurement/legal. Rishi, if you can provide the latency/throughput numbers by EOD, I'll stitch together the final proposal.

—Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
